title: Neuro-Symbolic Agentic AI for Networked Low-Altitude UAVs
neural_component: Neural grounding for uncertain observations and environment understanding, plus learned or reusable skill components.
symbolic_component: Explicit evidence conditions, neuro-symbolic planning, verification and metacognition, shared knowledge/memory, and task/goal management.
coupling_mechanism: Neural grounding informs symbolic reasoning and closed-loop agentic interaction; skills and mission completion are checked against explicit evidence conditions.
inclusion_rationale: Candidate direct UAV work: the abstract explicitly combines neural grounding, symbolic reasoning, and closed-loop agentic interaction for networked UAVs. Full-text review is still required before inclusion.
summary: Proposes neuro-symbolic agentic AI for networked low-altitude UAVs and illustrates an urban fire-inspection case in LAESim with verified image-delivery skills and evidence conditions.
limitations: Abstract-level review only. The paper describes a reference architecture and a simulation case; quantitative, hardware-in-the-loop, or real-flight evidence was not established in this record.

title: NEUROSYMLAND: Neuro-Symbolic Landing-Site Assessment for Robust and Edge-Deployable UAV Autonomy
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Software Engineering, Vol. 3, FSE, Article FSE146, July 2026
neural_component: Lightweight onboard perception that constructs a probabilistic semantic scene graph from visual input.
symbolic_component: Explicit symbolic safety constraints over the probabilistic scene graph for terrain flatness, obstacle clearance, and spatial consistency.
coupling_mechanism: Perception produces a probabilistic scene graph; symbolic constraints evaluate candidate landing regions over that explicit representation.
inclusion_rationale: Candidate direct UAV work: neural perception and explicit symbolic safety reasoning are functionally coupled for landing-site assessment. Full-text review and venue conflict resolution are required before inclusion.
summary: NEUROSYMLAND combines lightweight perception with explicit safety reasoning over a probabilistic semantic scene graph, reports 61/72 successful simulated assessments and 100 hardware-in-the-loop trials, and profiles edge-resource usage.
limitations: Abstract-level review only. Reported evidence is simulation and hardware-in-the-loop, not real flight. The arXiv page has conflicting publication comments (IROS 2026 versus FSE/PACMPL journal reference).
evidence: arXiv abs page on 2026-09-20: Comments say 'Accepted to the IROS 2026'; Journal reference says 'roceedings of the ACM on Software Engineering, Vol. 3, FSE, Article FSE146, July 2026'; Related DOI is 10.1145/3808153. Conflict recorded.
